title: Ad Hominem Fallacy Example
skills: identify attacks on a person that substitute for addressing an argument
distinguish relevant criticism from irrelevant personal attacks
evaluate arguments for logical relevance and sound reasoning
alignment_note: Provides an example of the ad hominem fallacy, in which an argument is dismissed by attacking the person rather than addressing the claim or evidence. Supports logical-fallacy recognition, rhetorical analysis, critical thinking, civil discourse, and evaluation of arguments across high school English courses.
